content:
Burnley Borough Council paid Beachcroft LLP a total of £4,406,071 across just 6 transactions between 2021/22 and 2023/24 — an average of £734,345 per payment. The supplier name in the spending data is "BEACHCROFT LLP", which is the former trading name of DAC Beachcroft LLP (Companies House OC317852), one of the UK's leading insurance litigation firms. A separate entity, DAC Beachcroft Claims Limited (04218278), operates as a solicitor practice from the same address at 25 Walbrook, London EC4N 8AF.

INV-007: The £3.2 Million Single Payment

The spending data reveals a stark pattern. In 2023/24, a single payment of £3,196,923 was made to Beachcroft LLP — representing 73% of all payments ever made to this supplier. The data shows it was categorised under Planning & Transportation, suggesting it relates to a capital project or construction matter rather than routine legal advice.

DAC Beachcroft specialises in insurance defence work, particularly construction and engineering disputes, professional indemnity claims, and public sector insurance. Their website describes dedicated teams for construction defect claims, subrogated recoveries, and insurance coverage disputes. This strongly suggests the £3.2M payment is an insurance-related settlement or legal costs arising from a construction claim.

The Payment Pattern

The growth from an average of £301,727 in 2021/22 to £3,196,923 in 2023/24 represents a 960% increase — flagged by our automated supplier lifecycle analysis as one of the most extreme spending escalations across all Burnley suppliers.

The December 2021 Payments

In December 2021, three payments totalling approximately £1.177 million were made to Beachcroft LLP. This timing is significant: Burnley Council completed its £20.7M acquisition of Charter Walk shopping centre in October 2021. These payments could relate to:

  • Insurance or legal due diligence costs for the Charter Walk acquisition
  • A separate construction claim settlement running concurrently
  • Insurance-related costs for Pioneer Place (construction started January 2022)

What Construction Project?

Several major Burnley Council construction projects were active in this period:

  • Pioneer Place — £23M cinema and leisure development. Eric Wright Construction was the contractor, with Maple Grove Developments as the developer. Completed summer 2023. The project was scaled back from the original design due to COVID-19 impacts and cost pressures.
  • Charter Walk — Acquired October 2021 for £20.7M. Legal support was provided by Geldards LLP (not Beachcroft), but insurance-related claims on the building could involve Beachcroft.
  • Vision Park — Employment land development by Trebor/Barnfield Construction, completed 2017-18. Any latent defect claims would be within the typical 6-year limitation period.

The timing of the October 2023 payment — just as Pioneer Place was completed and handed over by Eric Wright Construction — is consistent with a final account settlement or defects-related insurance claim. An Executive committee meeting was scheduled for 24 October 2023, the same month as the £3.2M payment.

Both entities share the registered office at 25 Walbrook, London EC4N 8AF. The LLP was formerly known as Beachcroft LLP (renamed October 2011), which matches the "BEACHCROFT LLP" name in the spending data.

No Contract on File

Despite receiving £4.4 million, Beachcroft LLP has no contract listed in the council's published contracts register. Under the Local Government Transparency Code, all contracts over £5,000 should be published. This is a transparency failure — whether the payments are legal fees, insurance pass-throughs, or settlement costs, the nature and terms of the engagement should be publicly documented.

Statement of Accounts

The 2024/25 Statement of Accounts was approved by the Audit and Standards Committee on 24 February 2026. The 2023/24 accounts received a positive audit opinion with no material misstatements. However, the specific provisions note and contingent liabilities disclosure — which would detail any insurance or construction claims — requires examination of the full accounts PDF. The accounts are published at burnley.gov.uk.

Key Questions

  1. What construction project or insurance claim generated the £3,196,923 payment in October 2023?
  2. Was this a settlement, legal fees, or an insurance pass-through (like Geldards' Pioneer Place payments)?
  3. What was the relationship between the December 2021 payments (£1.18M) and the Charter Walk acquisition?
  4. Why does the council's contracts register contain no entry for a £4.4M supplier?
  5. What provisions or contingent liabilities are disclosed in the 2023/24 accounts relating to construction claims?
  6. Was the October 2023 Executive meeting agenda item related to this payment?

Recommended FOI Request

A Freedom of Information request should seek: (1) the nature and purpose of all payments to Beachcroft LLP / DAC Beachcroft since 2021; (2) whether any relate to insurance claims or construction dispute settlements; (3) copies of any Executive or Audit Committee reports authorising these payments; (4) the provisions note from the 2023/24 Statement of Accounts.

Investigation INV-007. All figures derived from publicly available Burnley Borough Council spending data. Companies House data verified 10 April 2026. DAC Beachcroft LLP and DAC Beachcroft Claims Ltd are both active entities at Companies House.
